findings.statement: TNFa pathway activity is higher in non-responders to ustekinumab (t [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.t_nr_vs_r=4.79]), and also in the golimumab, infliximab and vedolizumab arms (all below the BH threshold), so it is a shared inflammatory-burden signal rather than drug-specific.

The UNIFI placebo arm also separates non-responders on TNFa activity (t [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).t_nr_vs_r=3.5]), so this marks severity, whereas the PURSUIT placebo arm shows nothing (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (PURSUIT).padj=0.932]).

NFkB activity is higher in infliximab non-responders (t [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.infliximab.t_nr_vs_r=5.14]) and shows the same pattern as TNFa across arms, including the UNIFI placebo arm, so it is not a drug-specific mechanism.

JAK-STAT activity is associated with non-response in ustekinumab (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0124]) and infliximab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.infliximab.padj=0.0284]) but not golimumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.204]) or vedolizumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.571]); the UNIFI placebo arm is borderline (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0543]).

TGFb activity is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (t [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.t_nr_vs_r=3.98]) and infliximab, but not in golimumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.348]); the UNIFI placebo arm is also significant, indicating partial severity.

OSM is higher at baseline in ustekinumab non-responders (difference [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.diff_nr_minus_r=0.651], BH padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]) but the drug-vs-placebo interaction is not significant (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.982]), the golimumab and infliximab arms do not survive correction, and the UNIFI placebo difference is similar (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]), so OSM is not shown to be a drug-specific mechanism.

TREM1 is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (difference [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.diff_nr_minus_r=0.826], BH padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000474]) but also in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234]), with no significant interaction; this marks severity, not an ustekinumab mechanism.

Baseline IL23A is not associated with ustekinumab response (BH padj [gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]); nothing survives correction in any arm, so the drug's target transcript does not stratify response.

CXCL8, third in the convergence ranking, is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (difference [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.diff_nr_minus_r=1.115], BH padj [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000102]) but the UNIFI placebo difference is larger ([gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).diff_nr_minus_r=1.3]), indicating a severity marker.

CXCR2, the top convergence gene with several clinical-stage antagonists, is associated with ustekinumab non-response (difference [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.diff_nr_minus_r=0.967], BH padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-6]) but equally in UNIFI placebo (difference [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).diff_nr_minus_r=1.008]); the neutrophil axis tracks severity.

ITGB7 baseline expression is not associated with vedolizumab response (BH padj [gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.995]) or with any other arm; no integrin-based stratification is supported.

IDO1 does not survive correction in ustekinumab (padj [gene=IDO1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.14]) and is significant only in UNIFI placebo non-responders (difference [gene=IDO1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).diff_nr_minus_r=1.108], padj [gene=IDO1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0289]), so it is a severity signal rather than a drug-response marker.

CHRDL2 is the strongest first-in-class discovery candidate (meta log2FC [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; meta_log2fc=2.36], up in all eight cohorts), but only a fraction of the signal is retained after composition correction ([gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.276]), flagged partly composition.

CHRDL2 transcripts are stromal, mostly inflammatory fibroblasts (lineage share [gene=CHRDL2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.939]), replicated in a second dataset; its highest vital-organ RNA ([gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=42.6] nTPM) is the highest among the screened candidates examined, a safety question; no clinical drug exists and only antibody tractability is listed.

LAX1 is a lymphocyte candidate with low vital-organ RNA ([gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=2.5] nTPM) but only a minority of its change is retained after composition correction ([gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.230]), consistent with infiltrating immune cells rather than a tissue change.

LAX1 transcripts are assigned to the T/NK lineage in the first single-cell dataset (lineage share [gene=LAX1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.454]), although the single largest cluster is plasma cells; the second dataset assigns plasma lineage, so the lineage call did not replicate, and no clinical drug or selective dependency is shown.

caveats: Response labels come from small cohorts for golimumab, infliximab and vedolizumab; most arms do not survive BH correction, so absence of signal is not evidence of no effect.
Drug-vs-placebo interactions were not significant for any gene examined.
All first-in-class candidates are partly composition-driven, so immune/stromal infiltration may explain the upregulation.
Associations only, not predictions; the discovery candidates were not tested for response, and only CHRDL2 and LAX1 were profiled in depth.
